findings.description: In the async retry_any.__ror__, the flatten check tests isinstance(other, retry_all) instead of retry_any. A retry_any on the left is never flattened, and a retry_all on the left is wrongly flattened into a retry_any.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`. The code returns retry_any(a, b, c, d), which changes the semantics from (a AND b) OR c OR d to a OR b OR c OR d. The sync version of this method correctly checks retry_any. The same flaw exists for the retry_all.__rand__ check on line 134, which tests retry_all correctly, so only the __ror__ check is wrong. The user sees retries happening in cases the combined condition should not allow.
